terms.comment: Quō īmus? — Cūr?: the boy’s own travel questions in the libellī.
evidence: Cic. Att. 16.6.2: cūr ego tēcum nōn sum?
Mart. 13.14.2: dīc mihi, cūr nostrās inchoat illa dapēs?
Catull. 85.1: quārē id faciam, fortasse requīris

terms.grammar: phrase: ob with the accusative of the relative

evidence: Ter. And. 979: Quid stās? quid cessās?
terms.comment: The impatient “why”: “what are you standing there for?”. Quid ita?, why so?

phrases.latin: cūr ego tēcum nōn sum? cūr ocellōs Ītaliae, vīllulās meās, nōn videō?
phrases.english: Why am I not with you? Why can’t I see the jewels of Italy, my little country houses?

phrases.latin: quid rīdēs? mūtātō nōmine dē tē fābula narrātur
phrases.english: why are you laughing? Change the name, and the story is about you

phrases.latin: clūdere quae cēnās lactūca solēbat avōrum, dīc mihi, cūr nostrās inchoat illa dapēs?
phrases.english: lettuce used to end our grandfathers’ dinners: tell me, why does it begin ours?

phrases.latin: ōdī et amō. quārē id faciam, fortasse requīris. nesciō, sed fierī sentiō et excrucior
phrases.english: I hate and I love. Why do I do it, perhaps you ask. I don’t know, but I feel it happening, and I am in torment

sources: Lewis & Short: cur · Lewis & Short: quare · Lewis & Short: ob (quam ob rem) · Lewis & Short: quis
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-terentius, loci-cicero-epistulae, loci-horatius, loci-martialis, loci-catullus), checked against the editions named there.
The comment on cūr comes from the grouped card.
